Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
---
 kernel/workqueue.c | 2 ++
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)

diff --git a/kernel/workqueue.c b/kernel/workqueue.c
index e163e7a7f5e5..ecdd5e6f2166 100644
--- a/kernel/workqueue.c
+++ b/kernel/workqueue.c
@@ -4194,6 +4194,8 @@ struct workqueue_struct *alloc_workqueue(const char *fmt,
 	return wq;
 
 err_free_wq:
+	wq_unregister_lockdep(wq);
+	wq_free_lockdep(wq);
 	free_workqueue_attrs(wq->unbound_attrs);
 	kfree(wq);
 	return NULL;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The root cause of the bug was a use-after-free and a memory leak in the error handling path of the `alloc_workqueue()` function. When the allocation of a workqueue failed, the code did not properly unregister and free the lock dependency keys associated with the workqueue, leading to a situation where the memory for these keys was accessed after it had already been freed. This resulted in a use-after-free error, as indicated by the KASAN (Kernel Address Sanitizer) reports. The patch added calls to `wq_unregister_lockdep(wq)` and `wq_free_lockdep(wq)` to ensure that the lock dependency keys are correctly cleaned up before freeing the workqueue structure itself.

The root cause of the bug was a use-after-free and a memory leak in the error handling path of the `alloc_workqueue()` function. When the allocation of a workqueue failed, the code did not properly unregister and free the lock dependency keys associated with the workqueue, leading to a situation where the memory for these keys was accessed after it had already been freed. This resulted in a use-after-free error, as indicated by the KASAN (Kernel Address Sanitizer) reports. The patch added calls to `wq_unregister_lockdep(wq)` and `wq_free_lockdep(wq)` to ensure that the lock dependency keys are correctly cleaned up before freeing the workqueue structure itself.
